identity: A single hadith with its full isnad - Sahih al-Bukhari, Kitab al-Iman: Said b. Yahya b. Said al-Qurashi > his father > Abu Burda b. Abd Allah b. Abi Burda > Abu Burda > Abu Musa al-Ashari, on which Islam is best. 44 tokens, no <NL>.
law: HADITH / ISNAD (section L). L1: the chain breaks after each transmission link - the boundary falls on the narrators name, BEFORE the qala that introduces the next link. Then the matn is segmented as speech: the question with its qalu, the answer with its qala. 44 tokens / 5 units = 8.8 per unit.
reasoning: L1 was learned in batch 1 from doc_27a114d4e376 @1 (haddathana Ismail | qala haddathani Malik b. Anas an ammihi Abi Suhayl...), where gold cut asyndetically after the first narrator. That is exactly this shape, three times over: @6 after al-Qurashi, @9 after abi, and @28 after Abi Musa radiya allah anhu. The an-links do NOT cut - L1 says the break follows a transmission VERB, and an is a preposition, so an Abi Burda an Abi Musa rides inside the haddathana Abu Burda unit; that is also why the third unit is the longest (19 tokens). In the matn I applied 1v rather than the announcer law: qala qalu ya rasul allah ayy al-islam afdal is ONE unit (the speech verb keeps its quotation when the quote runs on the same line), and so is qala man salima al-muslimuna min lisanihi wa-yadihi. I refused a boundary at @29 that would leave a bare one-token qala - the 0l precedent for a bare announcer as its own unit required the speech to start on the NEXT printed line, and there is no line structure here at all. The final wa-yadihi is bare-noun coordination inside the answer.
